topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and the exact operation-path joining rule
questions: Are user information, query strings, fragments, percent escapes, multiple trailing slashes and non-root base paths allowed, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path?
Which api_base_url shapes are valid, and what exact URL results when the base contains a path, query, fragment, user information or multiple trailing slashes?
Which components may `api_base_url` contain, and what exact joining rule applies to every accepted base URL?

judgement.why: This is the same api_base_url grammar and joining question previously assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Valid api_base_url forms, normalization, and path joining
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: What filesystem access sandboxed function code has, especially within the exchange directory
questions: May agent code freely create, read and modify files inside the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner for transporting declared inputs and outputs?
May agent-written code read or write the exchange directory or inspect files in the runtime, and if so, what filesystem access is permitted beyond the input values passed to run?
May function code create, read and modify arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or is filesystem access limited to kernel-created representations of its inputs and outputs?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about filesystem access available to sandboxed function code.

precedent.topic: Filesystem access allowed to sandboxed agent code
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Whether determinism is guaranteed and how nondeterministic APIs and divergent executions are handled
questions: How must the kernel make deterministic execution true for all admitted code, and what happens when equal executions produce different outputs?
Are all unlisted clock and nondeterminism sources forbidden, or are only the explicitly listed entry points trapped despite the no-clock and repeatability requirements?
Is byte-for-byte repeatability a guaranteed sandbox invariant, merely a test of conforming functions, or only an expectation used when evaluating a particular implementation?
Is repeatable output a guaranteed sandbox property, and if so what additional APIs or language features are prohibited or controlled to make it enforceable?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about whether and how the sandbox guarantees deterministic execution.

precedent.topic: Determinism requirement and sandbox enforcement property
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Which hosts qualify for the plain-HTTP loopback exception and how that is verified
questions: Does the exception cover only literal loopback IP addresses, hostnames such as `localhost`, or any hostname currently resolving to loopback, and must the connected address be rechecked?
Which hosts qualify for the loopback exception, and is the decision made from URL text or DNS results?
Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, or also names such as `localhost`, DNS names resolving to loopback, IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses and other loopback notations?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about identifying and verifying loopback hosts.

precedent.topic: Determination and DNS safety of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Exact multipart wire encoding and handling of unsafe multipart port names
questions: What exact multipart wire encoding is used, and which port names are refused or escaped before being placed in Content-Disposition?
How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text and other unsafe characters in multipart port names handled?

judgement.why: This repeats the multipart framing and unsafe-name encoding question previously assigned to a later state.

precedent.topic: Multipart field-name and media-type encoding and framing
precedent.why: Multipart header escaping, media-type grammar, boundary generation and wire framing are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Filesystem conditions that define a private data directory
questions: Which ownership, permission, file-type and ancestor-directory conditions constitute a private data directory?
What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions make the data directory and its contents private?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about the filesystem conditions denoted by private.

precedent.topic: Ownership and permission requirements for the data directory and files
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: How sandbox stdout and stderr are bounded and how unbounded writes are handled
questions: Where do stdout and stderr go, are their bytes bounded or counted, and which outcome results if code writes indefinitely?
What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr?

judgement.divergence: One implementer redirects and drains stdout and stderr without counting them, allowing a printing function to finish normally; another connects them to bounded or undrained pipes, causing large writes to produce resource_exhausted or block until timeout. The owner and agent notice the different execution outcome and trace, and a host operator may also notice output if an implementation inherits host streams.
judgement.why: The texts exclude printed output from failure_detail and output_bytes but never define its destination, drainage or resource accounting.

topics.topic: Outcome and byte accounting for function output that cannot be canonically encoded
questions: Which execution outcome applies when a function returns a value that cannot be represented by JCS?
How is `output_bytes` measured, and which outcome wins, when the returned object cannot be canonically encoded or does not have the required output shape?

quotes: execute_function: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the wall deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the channel recorded any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the module failed to load, has no run, raised, or the process exited abnormally; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, a value output cannot be serialized to canonical JSON, a file output is not bytes, a many output is not a list, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value ceiling and the spool ceilings are not the sandbox's: the module that stores or spools an output applies them after the execution has otherwise succeeded.
judgement.why: The later sandbox contract classifies a value that cannot be serialized to canonical JSON as contract_violation after higher-priority timeout, resource and sandbox checks.

topics.topic: Required coverage of trial-case input and expected-output ports, including absent versus empty expectations
questions: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output port, may it assert only a subset, and is an empty expected-output object distinct from absence?
Must inputs contain exactly every input port and no extras, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every output port, or may expected outputs be partial?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about required and permitted trial-case port coverage.

precedent.topic: Required and permitted port coverage in authored trial cases
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Whether binding port schemas must use the supported schema subset and when that is checked
questions: Must binding input and output schemas belong to the supported JSON Schema subset, and where does that check occur in the proposal's first-failure order?
Must every proposed binding port schema be validated against the kernel's supported schema subset, and where does that check occur in the proposal and acceptance order?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously answered question about unsupported schemas on operation-binding ports.

precedent.topic: Supported JSON Schema subset for operation-binding ports
quotes:
Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.
precedent.why: State 6 specifies that contracts refuse unsupported schemas while binding and flow ports may contain them but can never deliver a fitting value.

topics.topic: Whether seeded pseudorandomness is allowed in sandboxed function code
questions: May function code use a seeded pseudorandom generator, or must every randomness API be forbidden?
Does “no randomness” prohibit every random-number API, or only entropy-dependent and nondeterministic randomness?

judgement.why: This is the same previously answered question about explicitly seeded pseudorandom generators.

precedent.topic: Whether seeded pseudorandom APIs are permitted
quotes:
`random.Random(seed)`
   with an explicit seed stays usable: it draws no entropy, so equal inputs
   still give equal outputs, which is what State 0's "no randomness" asks.
precedent.why: The text explicitly permits explicitly seeded deterministic pseudorandom generation and explains that the prohibition concerns entropy-based nondeterminism.

topics.topic: Whether standing grants may target function nodes and when such requests are rejected
questions: Is a grant request for a function node refused, and if so at which check and with what governing condition?
Must a grant request naming a function node be refused, and at which check in the grant operation's order?

quotes:
`unknown_reference` for a flow that does not exist; `refused` when the flow has
no active version, for a node not in it (A10 rule 5), a function node, or a
`destructive` node.
judgement.why: The later public API explicitly refuses a grant request for a function node after the unknown-flow, missing-active-version and node-membership checks represented by the listed order.

topics.topic: Atomicity and validation order when mapped-node aggregate outputs exceed storage limits
questions: If a mapped node has several used outputs and one aggregate exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, can another output already be delivered or consumed, and in what order are aggregate outputs checked?

topics.topic: Behavior when approving a stale request preview
questions: What exactly does the approve action do and return when the approved preview no longer matches the rebuilt request?

topics.topic: Caller-visible outcome when sandbox cleanup cannot be confirmed
questions: What observable result does the caller receive when sandbox cleanup cannot be confirmed before the process stops?

topics.topic: Disclosure classification of guard-controlled values and guard-derived metadata
questions: When a personal-data guard controls an otherwise lower-class edge, what class applies to the delivered value and to guard-derived trace/output metadata visible to an agent?

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guard values
questions: What equality determines guard delivery and whether two guard values are different, especially for numbers, arrays and objects?

topics.topic: Exact canonical JSON value hashed for declared idempotency-key fields
questions: What exact JSON value is hashed when one or more idempotency-key fields are declared?

topics.topic: Exact trailing bytes removed from credential files
questions: Exactly which trailing bytes are removed from a credential file?

topics.topic: HTTP wire encoding requirements for non-ASCII header values
questions: How are non-ASCII header values serialized on the HTTP wire, or must all header names and values be ASCII?

topics.topic: How ProofResult represents failures without a node or edge subject
questions: How does ProofResult identify failures whose subject is not a node or edge?

topics.topic: How disclosure classes are computed for cyclic graphs without rooted sources
questions: How is the reachable disclosure class computed for a cyclic graph, especially a closed cycle with no rooted flow input, constant or operation output?

topics.topic: How manifests are resolved by revision and when invalid repositories or revisions fail
questions: How does the kernel resolve a manifest file at a revision, and when is a missing or invalid repository/revision detected?

topics.topic: How resource-limit violations are detected when function code catches the resulting errors
questions: How does the parent determine that memory or process limits were hit when Python receives and catches `MemoryError` or an OS error and then returns a valid result?

topics.topic: Legal port cardinalities and schemas for HTTP path and query placement
questions: Which cardinality/schema combinations are legal for path placeholders and query parameters, including a `many` path port or a `many` port whose element schema is itself an array?

topics.topic: MCP transport, protocol version, authentication, and request-byte accounting
questions: Which MCP transport and protocol version are used, where is the token carried, and exactly which serialized bytes count toward `surface_request_bytes_max`?

topics.topic: Meaning and validity of an absent manifest idempotency_key
questions: Does an absent idempotency_key mean no key, or is the manifest operation invalid, particularly for a non-read operation?

topics.topic: Order of trial-case size, shape, schema, expected-output, and media-type validation
questions: Is size checked per input port before expected outputs are validated, or only after all input and expected-output shape/schema checks, and where does file media-type validation occur?

topics.topic: Ordering of digest comparison and other checks when rechecking an accepted binding
questions: If the digest differs and the changed entry also fails another proposal check against the stored ports, which failure wins, and at what point in rule 5's order is digest comparison performed?

topics.topic: Representation of raw JSON-body bytes in the approval request digest
questions: How are raw JSON-body bytes represented inside the canonical JSON request description before hashing?

topics.topic: Startup validation precedence and mutations permitted before failure
questions: When several startup conditions fail, which check is reported first, and which checks or mutations may occur before that failure?

topics.topic: Total ordering of duplicate-endpoint edges and constants for identity and first-failure selection
questions: How are edges with identical endpoints but different guards, and multiple constants for the same destination, totally ordered for identity and first-failure selection?

topics.topic: Unicode code points treated as credential control characters
questions: Which Unicode code points count as control characters for credential validation?

topics.topic: Unit and truncation stage used for redacted failure-detail length
questions: Is the reported length counted in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation?

topics.topic: Validation and parsing semantics for a declared read-operation idempotency key
questions: What happens when a read operation's non-null `idempotency_key` is not a string, and are empty or repeated split parts retained exactly?

topics.topic: Where the run-pinned FlowActivation is recorded for later recovery
questions: Where is the exact FlowActivation pinned at run start recorded so it can be recovered unambiguously after later activations or a restart?

topics.topic: Whether a many-valued service output validates its array or each array element against value_schema
questions: For a `many` value output, must the response member be an array whose elements validate against `value_schema`, or must the array itself validate directly against `value_schema`?

topics.topic: Whether an incomplete HTTP body after final headers constitutes a valid final response
questions: Once a final status line and headers have arrived, does that status determine the effect outcome despite an incomplete body, or does incomplete framing mean no valid final response and therefore `outcome_unknown` for a non-read effect?

topics.topic: Whether empty node identifiers are allowed and how they affect proof ordering
questions: Is an empty node_id forbidden, or how are a real node with that id and a flow endpoint distinguished when ordering otherwise equal edge keys and selecting the first failure?

topics.topic: Whether repair evidence includes only the current contract version or historical versions
questions: Are the returned contract, trial cases and TrialExecutions limited to the current contract version, or are historical contract versions and their corpora also included?

topics.topic: Whether the prohibition on interpreting agent-supplied names also prohibits serializing them
questions: Is A16 intended to prohibit only evaluation and template interpretation, or does it also prohibit serializing names into outbound requests?

topics.topic: Whether transformed or encoded credentials may be exposed as ordinary service outputs
questions: May a transformed or encoded credential be stored and returned as an ordinary service output, or must the kernel uphold the absolute State 0 prohibition?

topics.topic: Which NodeExecution statuses are terminal versus retryable
questions: Which NodeExecution statuses conclude the element permanently, and which conclude only an attempt while leaving the element retryable?

topics.topic: Which lowered resource ceilings apply to pre-existing artifacts after an upgrade
questions: After an upgrade lowers code, stored-value, fixture, spool, response, request or text ceilings, which limits govern existing implementations, cases, constants, flows and newly started runs using them?

topics.topic: Which prior implementations are eligible for rollback
questions: Does rollback accept every non-current implementation with the required verdict, only an implementation created before the current one, or only one that appears earlier in activation history?
